method: CourtListener opinion text. No statutory publisher was reachable; every publisher, agency and mirror host returns 403 at the egress proxy, and WebFetch fails the same way on every host. Re-measured 2026-08-18.
queries: Brinker meal period employer obligation provide relieve duty rest break

assertions.text: a paid ten (10) minute rest period for every four (4) hours worked or major fraction thereof
assertions.note: This reproduces the wage order's raw words without the construction that says what they mean. Brinker settled it: 10 minutes for shifts of three and one-half to six hours, 20 minutes for shifts over six and up to ten, 30 minutes over ten and up to fourteen. The Court of Appeal had read the same words to give a seven-hour shift only 10 minutes, and the Supreme Court reversed that reading. A reader applying the clause as written can land on the rejected answer.

assertions.text: rest periods may not be combined with meal periods or waived in exchange for leaving early
assertions.note: No located opinion states this as a rule. Brinker addressed rest break TIMING and declined to impose a rigid sequence, which is a different question. Recorded as unverified rather than contradicted — absence of evidence, not evidence of error — but the clause states it flatly and nothing found supports it.

assertions.text: taken as close to the middle of the work period as practicable
assertions.note: Brinker treats this as the wage order's directive, subject to practical exceptions.

gaps: The clause gives the 'every four hours or major fraction' formula and no schedule, so it carries the ambiguity Brinker resolved without carrying the resolution.

sources.title: CourtListener — Brinker Restaurant Corp. v. Superior Court, 53 Cal.4th 1004 (2012)

judicialQuotations.case: Brinker Restaurant Corp. v. Superior Court (Cal. 2012)
judicialQuotations.quote: We conclude that under Wage Order No. 5 and Labor Code section 512, subdivision (a), an employer must relieve the employee of all duty for the designated period, but need not ensure that the employee does no work.

judicialQuotations.case: Brinker Restaurant Corp. v. Superior Court (Cal. 2012)
judicialQuotations.quote: The combined effect of the two pertinent sentences, giving full effect to each, is this; Employees are entitled to 10 minutes' rest for shifts from three and one-half to six hours in length, 20 minutes for shifts of more than six hours up to 10 hours, 30 minutes for shifts of more than 10 hours up to 14 hours, and so on.

singleOpinionCaveat: One opinion, but it is the California Supreme Court construing the statute and the wage order directly, which is the strongest thing this channel can produce. It still does not meet the two-primary standard and upgrades nothing.
